name: Changi Chapel
reason: Rule 2: small heritage chapel built by POWs at Changi, moved to Duntroon; Wikivoyage Canberra and North Canberra both name it (halfway along Miles Road) as military tourism, so a visitor source names a landmark. One listing, inside RMC Duntroon grounds.
objection: Short visit, one source repeated across two pages, sits inside Royal Military College grounds where most buildings are restricted; may be part of a Duntroon visit rather than a draw.

name: Australian Defence Force Academy
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage says the grounds are open but 'of little interest to travellers'; only an annual open day is offered.
objection: The library has military history collections and occasional exhibitions, but that is not a visitor draw.

name: Duntroon Dairy
reason: Rule 3/2: Wikivoyage lists it as believed to be the oldest standing building in the ACT, viewable from a small car park with signage and lake views, but open only on request.
objection: Exterior view of about 15 minutes with one source; keeping adds a minor heritage stop. Against: no interior access.

name: Yowani Country Club

name: Stage 88

objection: Hosts the Floriade site, but that is an annual event not a permanent attraction.

name: St John the Baptist Church, Reid
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage (North Canberra and Canberra) and VisitCanberra's 100 things all name Canberra's oldest church (1845) and its small schoolhouse museum, so there is something to see inside; three counted sources.
objection: A short stop and it is a church; keep depends on the schoolhouse museum being open.
